concerns.text: T010c (derive effort data) and T012 (bias correction) are marked [P] (parallel-safe) but have explicit sequential dependencies: T010c depends on T010 output, and T012 depends on T010c output. Marking them as [P] implies they can run concurrently with other tasks, but they cannot run concurrently with their own producers. This violates the 'Producer before consumer' rule and creates a false parallelization signal.

T013 (filter/thin) lists dependencies on T010, T011, T012, and T015. However, T012 (bias correction) produces a raster (`bias_layer.tif`) that is not an input for T013 (which filters occurrence CSVs). T013 only needs the occurrence CSVs (T010, T011) and climate rasters (T015). Including T012 as a dependency creates a circular or unnecessary blocking dependency that prevents T013 from running as soon as its actual inputs are ready.

T029b (filter/thin recent data) is listed as a dependency for T028 (projection) and T029 (evaluation). However, T028 (projection) only requires trained models (T021-T023) and future climate rasters (T015b). It does NOT require the processed recent occurrence data (T029b). T029b is only needed for T029 (evaluation). Listing T029b as a dependency for T028 creates an artificial ordering constraint that blocks parallel execution of projection tasks.

T010 description includes 'Also implement logic to derive... effort data' AND T010c is a separate task to 'Implement logic... to derive effort data'. This splits the implementation of a single logical step (deriving effort data) across two tasks with ambiguous ownership. T010 should either do the derivation (removing T010c) or T010c should be the sole task for derivation, with T010 strictly downloading. The current split creates a 'producer' (T010) that partially emits the artifact T010c needs, violating clear producer/consumer boundaries.
